title: Vietnam eSIM: e-visa, arrival and travel data | Magic eSIM
description: Vietnam travel eSIM for mobile data: the e-visa open to all nationalities, free Wi-Fi at its international airports and 220 V sockets.
lead: What to sort out for Vietnam before you land: the e-visa, the first hour at the airport, and data for Vietnam alone or for a route that crosses into Cambodia.

paragraphs: Not everyone needs a visa. The government waives it for stays of up to 45 days for citizens of listed countries, including the United Kingdom, Germany, France, Japan, South Korea, the Netherlands and Switzerland, if they hold a return or onward ticket. The tourism board adds that flying straight into Phu Quoc from abroad allows up to 30 days on that island without a visa, but continuing to the rest of Vietnam needs a visa or an e-visa.

Since 15 August 2023, citizens of every country and territory have been able to apply for a Vietnamese e-visa, according to the Vietnam National Authority of Tourism. The Immigration Department issues it for up to 90 days, with a single entry or multiple entries.

Since 11 November 2024, the department's e-visa portal has run on two addresses, evisa.gov.vn and thithucdientu.gov.vn; the tourism board warns against unauthorised agencies that charge inflated fees. Your passport should be valid for at least six months after you arrive and have two blank pages.

The approval names the checkpoint you may enter through, so match it to your flight or crossing and keep it where you can open it at the border. On the Cambodian border, the land gates at Moc Bai, Xa Mat and Ha Tien are among the checkpoints open to e-visa holders.

sections.h2: Wi-Fi, SIM counters, cash and an eSIM
paragraphs: Vietnam's tourism board says all international airports in the country have free Wi-Fi, and that free public internet access is available in several tourist hubs as well as major airports. It publishes no sign-in details or time limits, so treat it as a way to send a first message rather than a plan for the transfer into town.

Prepaid local SIM cards are sold at the major airports and in shops, and the tourism board says you need to show your passport to register one. An eSIM is the other route: a profile you add to your phone, which needs a phone that supports eSIM and is not locked to your home network. The [compatibility guide](/en/guides/compatibility/) explains how to check both.

The tourism board says ATMs that take international cards stand just outside the arrival gates at all major airports, with exchange counters inside before the exit. The đồng is used in notes only, and coins are not in use; cash covers small purchases and street vendors, while hotels, restaurants and shops generally take cards.
Power is 220 V, and most sockets take plugs with two round prongs, so look at your charger's plug before you pack.

sections.h2: Vietnam only, or the wider region
paragraphs: Local plans cover Vietnam on its own and fit a trip that starts and ends in the country.

If your route crosses into Cambodia by bus or boat, regional plans that include Vietnam also cover Cambodia, Thailand, Malaysia, Singapore, the Philippines and Indonesia. Daily plans give you a fixed allowance per day, a fit for travellers who prefer to know what each day of the trip includes.
Check “Plans at a glance” above for how much data each plan offers and for how long; the [activation guide](/en/guides/activation/) covers what to check before you install a plan.

faq.q: Can I get an e-visa for Vietnam?
faq.a: The Vietnam National Authority of Tourism says citizens of all countries and territories have been able to apply since 15 August 2023. The Immigration Department's portal is at evisa.gov.vn and thithucdientu.gov.vn, and the e-visa runs for up to 90 days with a single entry or multiple entries. Citizens of countries on the government's waiver list, such as the United Kingdom, Germany and Japan, can instead stay up to 45 days without a visa if they hold a return or onward ticket.

faq.q: Can I enter Vietnam overland from Cambodia on an e-visa?
faq.a: Yes, at a checkpoint open to e-visa holders. The tourism board lists Moc Bai, Xa Mat and Ha Tien among the gates on the Cambodian border, and says the approval names your port of entry, so apply with the crossing you actually plan to use.

faq.q: Do I need a passport to buy a SIM card in Vietnam?
faq.a: For a local prepaid SIM card bought in Vietnam, yes: the tourism board says you need to show your passport to register it. Those cards are sold at the major airports and in shops.

faq.q: Is there free Wi-Fi at airports in Vietnam?
faq.a: According to the tourism board, all international airports in Vietnam have free Wi-Fi. It does not publish time limits or sign-in steps.

faq.q: Will one plan cover Vietnam and Cambodia?
faq.a: Regional plans that include Vietnam also cover Cambodia, as well as Thailand and the Philippines.

faq.q: Will I need a plug adapter in Vietnam?
faq.a: It depends on your plug. The supply is 220 V at 50 Hz and plug types A, B, C and F are in use; the tourism board says most sockets take two round prongs.
